results.title: Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a visitor's hat
results.content: Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo's much-loved hippopotamus, has died after swallowing a knitted hat that became stuck in her digestive system. Vets made several attempts to remove the object but were unable to save the nine-year-old animal.

results.title: Video shows isolated Awá Indigenous people make contact with government team in Brazil
results.content: Around 20 members of Brazil’s isolated Awá Indigenous group have approached a government outpost in the Amazon, asking for yams before returning to the forest. The rare encounter has raised concerns about their health and possible food shortages.

results.title: US: Protesters demand human control over AI after Anthropic's IPO
results.content: Protesters gathered outside Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters on 19 November 2026 to demand tighter regulation and greater human control over artificial intelligence, following the company’s $2 trillion stock market debut.

results.title: Japan: The dark secret behind an island paradise full of rabbits
results.content: Hundreds of rabbits roam freely on Japan's Okunoshima Island, delighting visitors from around the world. But behind its idyllic scenery lies a troubling history of secret chemical weapons production.

results.title: Ukraine: Kyiv metro stations become overnight shelters amid air raids
results.content: Residents of Kyiv, Ukraine, sought refuge in underground metro stations overnight on Thursday 19 November 2026, as repeated air raid alerts warned of further Russian attacks on the capital. Strikes on the Ukrainian capital killed at least one person, injured five and damaged two embassies.

results.title: 217-day underwater patrol of UK's nuclear submarine HMS Vengeance worries experts
results.content: The Royal Navy's HMS Vengeance nuclear submarine has set a new record by completing a 217-day mission. For about seven months, the crew had almost no contact with the outside world.

results.title: White House national cyber director fired after wave of tech outages
results.content: The national cyber director is tasked with advising the president on cybersecurity policy and strategy, including information security and data protection as well as deterrence of "malicious" activity.

results.content: The Trump administration pressed ahead with the auction despite a federal judge’s finding that regulators broke wildlife protection law and conservation groups vowed to have the leases voided.

results.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes damage Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv
results.content: Russian strikes damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv on Thursday. Windows were shattered and vehicles damaged, but diplomatic staff escaped unharmed.

results.title: US defence secretary Pete Hegseth lands in Ecuador on Latin America anti-narcotics tour
results.content: The US defence secretary, under fire for his role in the Iran war and illegal bombings in the Caribbean and Pacific, has announced a military pact with Venezuela. His next stop is Honduras.

results.title: At least one dead and dozens missing after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal en route to Spain
results.content: The latest sinking comes amid a sharp rise in departures towards the Canary Islands, with more than 11,000 people reaching the Spanish archipelago in the first two weeks of November.

results.title: New regional security architecture will also benefit Europe, Pakistani FM tells Euronews
results.content: In an exclusive interview for Euronews’ World Conversation show, Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister revealed the backstage mediation that brought the US and Iran to agreement in June. He also outlined Pakistan's strategy towards a new regional security architecture in coordination with Europe.

results.title: Trump leaves China without meeting Kim Jong-un as trilateral summit raises concerns across Asia
results.content: The US, Chinese and Russian leaders pledged to hold talks on nuclear risk reduction, but made no mention of North Korea in their joint peace declaration.

results.title: US: Protesters warn of AI bubble as Anthropic makes stock market history
results.content: Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut with a record-breaking IPO valuing the AI company at $1.5 trillion. Outside the exchange in New York, police detained three protesters warning of financial risks.

results.title: On board with Frontex: Euronews patrols the waters off Crete as migrant arrivals from Libya rise
results.content: Aboard the Latvian patrol vessel Valpas, Euronews follows maritime operations and visits a Frontex drone base at Tympaki airfield. A search for missing migrants near Chrissi Island highlights the dangers of the crossing, while temporary reception facilities face growing pressure.

results.title: Trump questions Europe's billions in Ukraine aid during surprise call
results.content: The US president reportedly called into a meeting of Kyiv's European allies from Air Force One, hours after talks with Putin and Xi, and said Moscow was ready to negotiate a peace deal.

results.content: Disruption to oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz is driving up costs for households, while the agency says the longer the crisis continues, the harder it will be for global energy markets to recover.

results.content: Pew Research Center has projected that both Islam and Christianity will grow between 2020 and 2070, with Muslims rising by more than 80% to over 3.6 billion and Christians by 30% to close to 3 billion.

results.content: Vladimir Putin says his meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping covered key global security issues, including the war in Ukraine, nuclear proliferation and freedom of navigation. results.title: Giving a solo founder the horsepower of a multinational — affordably
results.content: European small businesses have ambition and creativity, but lack time and budgets. As Kuo Zhang of Alibaba.com writes in an op-ed for Euronews, affordable, ready-to-use AI and global supply chain tools give even solo founders the capabilities of global companies, freeing them to focus on growth.

results.title: North Korea expanding original uranium enrichment facility, UN nuclear watchdog says
results.content: The IAEA has not had access to Yongbyon or other locations in North Korea since the country kicked out the agency’s inspectors in 2009.
